title: I'm working on Climbfolk - a turn-based roguelite RPG inspired by Pokémon, Hades, and Stardew Valley!
author: starcount_games
selftext:
I did it. I finally clicked that "Publish to Coming Soon" button. After all that waiting and bureaucracy, Climbfolk has a Steam page now!

So what is it about?

Climbfolk is a turn-based roguelite RPG that combines a few things that I love most about games like Pokémon, Hades, and Stardew Valley. You find and recruit heroes & companions; you go on runs that have random outcomes, and in between you can build your own little sky camp.

If you like the idea, you can wishlist and follow on Steam:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5625710/Climbfolk/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5625710/Climbfolk/?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAcGRvZgFicmlkETFlaGV2TENuaVdLT1hxeDFkc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABH1qZmz-LFdRzoLVImxZN20Q9s6t8cnWfvBDcwUdysORidSxwgl6NzcoTrSPt_aem_a6szFTmd1lLW0NTjiO-f6g)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/starcount_games please share some more about how you used AI in developing this. Naming the tools or saying "made with AI" doesn't count. Rule 4 is how we keep promotional posts contributing, by having them talk about the process and how the game was made. Trying to keep the sub focused on dev. This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: starcount_games
replies.body: AI tools were used to complete repetitive tasks like creating databases and configs, procedural generation, and battle simulations. Also, it was used to generate art concepts. Assets were created by me with LibreSprite.

comments.author: RBRgd
comments.body: I love the visual style and have been looking into solo developing an indie game myself. How long did it take to learn to make pixel art like this?

replies.author: starcount_games
replies.body:
Since I remember myself I loved drawing, but I was always very shy about it. I'm also not a professional artist. I am a biologist, who is passionate about video games. Pixel art can be easier to handle because you can control your streak pixel by pixel. It will take time though. My advice: just start. I wouldn't suggest taking long courses, just watch YouTube videos and learn, then post your art here, on Reddit, so people can give you feedback, once you are happy with the results.

I was also into programming before... But never tried to make an actual game. So...

The best advice is:

Just do it...
